prompt:
You are a credit rating analyst. Using only the information below and general knowledge predating 2026-02-04, assign the issuer a letter credit rating on the 21-grade scale below (finest granularity you can justify).
Valid answers (choose exactly one): AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-, CC, C.
Company information (as of 2026-02-04):
| Current ratio           | 0.59 |
| Retained earnings       | 36,413M |
| Current liabilities     | 21,864M |
| Current assets          | 12,951M |
| Shareholders' equity    | 25,838M |
| Total liabilities       | 45,596M |
| Total assets            | 71,487M |
| EBIT / operating income | 979M |
| Revenue                 | 10,496M |
Reason briefly in 1-3 sentences. Then, on a separate final line, output exactly:
DECISION: <one label>
raw_response:
The firm shows decent profitability (EBIT ~9.3% of revenue) but weak liquidity (current ratio ~0.59) and moderate-to-high leverage (total liabilities ≈ 45.6B vs equity 25.8B; debt/equity ≈ 1.77). On balance, credit risk appears elevated due to liquidity constraints, though scale and profitability support investment-grade rather than speculative grade. Therefore, a BBB rating is appropriate.

DECISION: BBB
